body:
Automatic opening vents (AOVs) are the roof hatches, façade windows, louvres and shaft dampers that open to let smoke out of a stair, lobby or corridor when the fire alarm calls for them. They are life-safety equipment, not comfort ventilation. iComply Property Services quotes AOV and smoke-control work across the UK from 17 Woodlands Park Road, Offerton, Stockport, Cheshire SK2 5DE. This hub explains the work and links to every AOV town page we publish. A town page is a place on our published list, not a depot, and every quote is price on application after the building has been described.

Most of the enquiries we see about automatic opening vents are for blocks of flats, care homes, schools and offices with a protected stair. The usual work falls into four kinds: a test of a system that is already installed, a repair to an actuator, panel or battery, a planned maintenance visit to a written schedule, and a new installation or upgrade where a fire strategy already names the vents. Each one is quoted separately because the access, the parts and the paperwork are different.

The references are the building's fire strategy, BS 9991 where a residential block was designed or refurbished to that code, BS 9999 for many other buildings, and the BS EN 12101 family for the products themselves: part 2 for natural smoke and heat exhaust ventilators, part 3 for powered fans and part 10 for power supplies. Naming a standard on this page is not a claim that we hold a scheme registration. We do not claim BAFE, FIRAS or approved-installer status for any brand, and we do not invent a free-area calculation to suit a vent that is already on site.

A test visit checks what actually moves. We trigger the fire-alarm input, or ask the alarm contractor to, and watch every vent the strategy names travel fully open. We open the manual break-glass or switch at each landing. We take the panel off mains to prove the batteries hold the vents for the standby period. We check that a rain or wind sensor cannot hold a smoke vent shut when the fire signal arrives. A green panel light with a seized roof lid is a fail, and the record says so.

Controls, actuators and batteries are the parts residents never see and the parts that fail quietly. Chain actuators seize, hinges drop, and batteries date out while a status lamp still looks healthy. On repair work we name the manufacturer, the actuator stroke and the battery capacity before ordering parts. A takeover of an existing system is offered only where the brand can still be supported. Mixing a new actuator onto a tired vent without measuring the stroke is how sashes get torn off their hinges.

The fire-alarm interface is part of the job whenever the strategy says the vent opens on a zone or a common alarm. We identify the panel, the output and the cause-and-effect line. If another contractor maintains the alarm, we still need a witnessed test, or the record states that the interface was not proved.

Roof and façade work needs access equipment, weather and a plan for an occupied building. A stair cannot be left open to the weather overnight because a hatch was removed and the weather turned. The sequence is agreed first: make safe, fit, prove, and only then leave. Scaffold or a mobile platform is written into the quote when the survey shows it is needed, not added on the day.

The responsible person keeps the duty. In England and Wales that is under the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005, and in England the Fire Safety (England) Regulations 2022 add checks and resident information for multi-occupied residential buildings. In Scotland the Fire (Scotland) Act 2005 applies. We leave a record of the visit that happened: what was tested, what moved, what did not and what we recommend. We do not take the statutory role and we do not turn a failed travel test into a pass.

Every AOV town page below covers the same service in that place, with local notes, frequently asked questions and contact details. Use the search box or the letters to find a town, a city or a county. If your town is not listed, the service is still quoted; send the postcode. Vehicle barrier towns have their own index, and the AOV service hub lists equipment and manufacturers.

To ask for a quote, send the postcode, the building type, the number of storeys and stairs, the panel brand if you can see it, and whether a vent is stuck open or shut. Photos of the panel, the vent and the roof access help. Phone or WhatsApp 07517806082, or email icomplypropertyservices@gmail.com. If a stair vent is stuck open or shut and people are in the building, say so when you call. We confirm the scope in writing before anyone is booked, and the figure is price on application once that scope is clear. We do not publish a reply-time or attendance-time promise.

faqs.a: Tests, repairs, maintenance and installation are price on application. The quote names the vents, the panel, the access and whether the job is test-only, repair or supply and fit. This page does not publish a fee.

AOV and smoke control is fire-protection work, so it is quoted across the UK from our Stockport workshop. The town pages below are the places we publish. If yours is not listed, send the postcode and we will say whether we can quote.

faqs.q: What happens on an AOV test visit?
faqs.a: We prove the fire-alarm input, open each vent the strategy names, try the manual controls at each landing, check battery standby with the mains off, and check that a rain or wind sensor cannot hold a smoke vent shut. The record lists what moved and what did not.

faqs.q: Do you hold a smoke-control scheme registration?
faqs.a: No. We do not claim BAFE, FIRAS or approved-installer status. Naming BS EN 12101 or BS 9991 on this page is not an accreditation. If your insurer or fire strategy requires a scheme member, tell us and we will say so before quoting.

faqs.q: Can you work on a system another company installed?
faqs.a: Often, yes, if the manufacturer's parts and information are still available. We name the brand on the quote. If the panel or actuator cannot be supported, the quote explains why and what the options are.

faqs.q: How do I send an AOV enquiry?
faqs.a: Phone or WhatsApp 07517806082, or email icomplypropertyservices@gmail.com. Send the postcode, the building type, the number of storeys and stairs, the panel brand and a photo. Correspondence goes to 17 Woodlands Park Road, Offerton, Stockport, Cheshire SK2 5DE.
